_doc: Why each toggle in `docs/EVAL_STATUS.md`'s `Unreachable by any screen` list is
not a gene. One line each, so the residual count is examined work rather than
an unexamined ceiling. `tools/test_genome_reach_debt.py` requires this file to
cover exactly that computed list: a toggle that becomes reachable must LOSE its
entry here, and a new unreachable toggle must gain one. Neither side can rot.
Groups: `bundle` turns other genes on; `host-only` cannot fire on a native
board; `live-bridge-row` could fire but a gene row would withhold it from the
live bridge; `production-on` ships on and a gene row would switch it off;
`configured-on` ships on from the wrong constructor for the table's own test;
`infrastructure` has no decision content; `already-on` would screen inert;

bank_envoys.reason: Screenable would mean WITHHELD. It has a `LIVE_TREATMENTS` row, so a `PRODUCTION_OPT_INS` row flips `ledger_default_on` from `None` to `Some(false)` and `apply_gene_ledger` would then take it out of the live bridge. That is a deployment change wearing an instrument's clothes. The move it wants is the door `culture-coverage` went through: out of `FIRAXIS_ONLY_TREATMENTS` and into an `ENGINE_REPAIR_*` half, taken deliberately with the bridge change owned and priced. What it does: the baseline envoy pass must not overwrite a deliberate bank. Its host-only classification is an argument about which rivals the weights were bred against, not a claim the code cannot fire natively.

camp_bounty.reason: A GENE ROW WAS WRITTEN FOR IT IN #2330 AND THE FIRES GATE REFUSED IT. Clearing a camp is a peacetime errand worth sending for, not only something a unit does when a camp is already in its way. A single-gene probe over 12 map pairs (72 matched seat comparisons, 24 games) left both arms byte-identical: win Δ, score-share Δ and both standard errors all exactly zero, which is the never-fired signature, not a null. The row was removed rather than shipped to consume a genome bit and return a zero-width interval. Evidence: `docs/gene_screens/fires/camp-bounty.json`. To wire it, make the behaviour reachable on the screen's board first, then re-probe.

live_barbarian_scouts_capture.reason: The native barbarian seat's recon units cannot capture a civilian (the minor-seat gate returns them to fortify before `capture_adjacent_civilian`; the engine's scout phase moves them by `relocate`, which has no capture hook), so counting a barbarian scout in the exact capture-reach models is a zero-width change on a native board and a screen row could only measure noise. The Civilization VI host's scouts DO capture — run civvis-20260828T122324Z lost four settlers to one — so this is a `Kind::HostOnly` gene priced by the live ladder's `settlers_captured` column, with `disable_live_barbarian_scouts_capture` as the withholding arm.

live_move_refusal_break.reason: The gene's whole proof is an issued step the NEXT turn's board shows untaken — the host's `did_not_move` answer read off the rebuilt mirror. In the simulator every legal applied move moves the unit, so the watch can never accumulate a strike, the bar can never be placed, and a screen row would be zero-width by construction. The live ladder prices it through the `did_not_move` share of `order_failed` (13.9% of all orders in the 2026-08-30 measurement), with `disable_live_move_refusal_break` as the withholding arm.

live_settler_capture_lessons.reason: Every rule under it answers a live-seat fact a native board does not have: settler ids that change on every export (the vanished-settler detector is fed by `remap_unit_memory`), the host's own movement flood disagreeing with the mirror's, camps and raiders walking out of a fog the native barbarian seat does not hunt through, and the native seat's civilian losses being ~zero to begin with. A screen row would be zero-width by construction; the live ladder prices it directly through `settlers_captured` (#2724), with `disable_live_settler_capture_lessons` as the withholding arm.
